summary: Longlian was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Fazun in 1939 and under Nenghai Shi from circa 1941 to 1967.

Lore Sander specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying under Ernst Waldschmidt (c. 1962–1967). She was a curator at the Museum of Asian Art (1987) and lectured at the Free University of Berlin (1994).

Lori Meeks works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned a BA from Columbia (c. 1994–1998) and a PhD from Princeton under Jacqueline I. Stone (c. 1998–2003), joining the University of Southern California faculty in 2004.

Lorna Dewaraja worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Ceylon (c. 1949–1953) and University of London (c. 1966–1970), later serving as Associate Professor of History at the University of Peradeniya.

Lothar Ledderose is a Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology scholar who completed his Habilitation at the University of Cologne (c. 1975–1976). He served as Professor at Heidelberg University (c. 1976–2010) and President of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1978–1990).

Lothar von Falkenhausen is a Sinologist and archaeologist who studied at Bonn, Peking University, and Harvard (MA c. 1981–1982; PhD c. 1982–1988). Since 1993, he has served as a Full Professor at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Louis Charles Casartelli was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He earned degrees from Ushaw College, the University of London, and KU Leuven under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin, later lecturing at the University of Manchester (1903–1920).

Louis Deroy was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at KU Leuven and the University of Paris. His career was based at the University of Liège, where he rose from chef de travaux in 1956 to full professor in 1972.

Louis Dubeux was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar who studied under Silvestre de Sacy and Chézy. He served at the Royal Danish Library, as Professor of Turkish at INALCO (1848–1849), and Professor of Hebrew at Collège de France (1857–1862).

Louis Dumont was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Marcel Mauss, Walther Schubring, and Pierre Meile, completing a PhD at the University of Paris. He taught at Oxford (1951–1955) and became Directeur d'Études at EPHE and EHESS in 1955.

Louis Dupree was a history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who earned a BA from Harvard (c. 1946–1949). He held posts at Pennsylvania State University (c. 1954–1959), UNC Chapel Hill (c. 1977–1989), and Duke University (c. 1985–1989).

Louis Duvau was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, EPHE, and Leipzig, working under Ferdinand de Saussure (c. 1885–1889). He held a post at the École française de Rome from 1887 to 1888.

Louis Finot was an Indologist and historian who studied under Sylvain Lévi at EPHE. He served as the first Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1899–1904) and held chairs at EPHE (1917–1930) and the Collège de France (1920–1930).
Louis Frédéric worked in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the Sorbonne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Louis Gabaude is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient circa 1980.

Louis Gernet was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (c. 1902–1905). He held long-term posts at the University of Algiers (c. 1917–1948) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (c. 1948–1962).

Louis H. Gray was an Indologist and linguist who studied under A. V. Williams Jackson at Columbia (PhD c. 1898–1900). He held professorships at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (1921–1926) and Columbia University (1926–1944).

Louis Hambis was a Sinologist and Central Asian studies scholar who studied under Paul Pelliot and at EPHE. He was a professor at the Collège de France (1965–1977) and directed the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises (1959–1973).
Louis Havet was a linguist who studied at EPHE under Michel Bréal, Gaston Paris, and Abel Bergaigne. He served as Professor of Latin Philology at the Collège de France from 1885 to 1925.

Louis Léon Duvau was a linguist who studied under Michel Bréal and Ferdinand de Saussure at Paris, Leipzig, and Rome. He taught classical philology at Burgundy (1887), comparative grammar at Lille (1888–1891), and became maître de conférences at EPHE in 1891.
